outline.description: Large pre-trained language models rarely perform well out‑of‑the-box when faced with specialized dialogue or domain tasks unless they are adapted through instruction following finetune. Traditional finetune updates every parameter and therefore consumes hundreds of gigabytes during training – a barrier that keeps most researchers away from tinkering with giant models.

Quantising neural network parameters reduces their storage footprint by converting costly floating point numbers into compact integer representations while preserving sufficient precision during inference.”
subtopics: Effect on bit budget per tensor

outline.chapter_title: Parameter Efficient Fine–Tuning via Low‐Rank Adapters
outline.description: Zeroing weights during finetune saves precious GPU resources if we rewrite every linear projection by means of two short matrices whose ranks are far smaller than their input/output dimensions.
subtopics: Activation momentum dominates Day Minute cost

outline.chapter_title: NormalFloat (NFk): A Distribution Aware Integer Data Type
outline.description: Pretrained transformer weights follow an approximately zero‐centred Gaussian distribution whose variability differs layerwise. By constructing an asymmetrical k‑bit data type based on exact Gaussian quantiles we attain superior empirical fidelity versus naïve Float/k‐bit integers.
